proof:
# Fine mesh larger than coarse mass: an exact crossed-triangle sequence

This is a genuine remaining regime for relative-mesh recovery. All
vertices are sampled, both coarse fibers have positive area, the
actual fine mixed hull is the entire body, and one block-affine
normalization gives a unit inball and a fixed outer ball. Nevertheless
delta_l/M_l tends to infinity. The exact fine maximal depth is also
computed. It stays ABOVE the OC target; this is not a counterexample
to that inequality.

## 1. Rational bodies with exact fine hulls

Let L>=6 be an integer divisible by three, and put

    h=1/L,         epsilon=h^2.

Use coordinates (z,u,x), with coarse z in Z, fine u in hZ, and
continuous x in R. At coarse bases zero and one set

    Q_0=conv{(-1,0),(1,-epsilon),(1,epsilon)},
    Q_1=conv{(-h,-1),(h,1),(0,2h)}                     (1)

in the (u,x)-plane, and let C_h be their lifted convex hull. Its only
coarse integer fibers are exactly Q_0,Q_1. Every vertex in (1) has
u/h an integer. Therefore, with

    S_h=C_h intersect (Z times hZ times R),

one has C_h=conv(S_h) EXACTLY: S_h contains every generating vertex,
and conversely S_h subset C_h. Equivalently, pulling back by
(z,k,x)->(z,hk,x) gives an actual standard n=2,d=1 mixed body.

Both triangles have area 2epsilon. For Q_1, the determinant of
(2h,2) and (h,1+2h) is 4h^2. Thus the coarse mixed area is

    M_h=|Q_0|+|Q_1|=4epsilon=4h^2>0.                    (2)

All original positive fine fibers have full continuous dimension one.
Zero-length boundary fibers remain part of S_h but carry zero H_1 mass.

## 2. Uniform roundness in a block-affine frame

The triangles contain the segments

    z=0: (u,x)=(t,0),   -1<=t<=1,
    z=1: (u,x)=(ht,t),  -1<=t<=1.

Their hull T_h is the image of the fixed tetrahedron

    T_0={0<=z<=1, |u|<=1-z, |x|<=z}

under the continuous shear (u,x)->(u+h x,x). This shear is used
ONLY to verify geometric inclusion; it is not applied to the fine
lattice. T_0 contains the ball of radius 1/(2sqrt(2)) about
b=(1/2,0,0), by its four facet distances. The inverse shear has
operator norm at most 1+h. Hence T_h, and therefore C_h, contains

    b+[1/(2sqrt(2)(1+h))] B_2^3 superset b+(1/4)B_2^3.

The last containment holds for h<=1/6. Also
C_h subset [0,1] times [-1,1]^2 subset b+(3/2)B_2^3.
The FIXED block-affine map

    F(z,u,x)=(4z-2,4u,4x)

therefore gives

    B_2^3 subset F(C_h) subset 6B_2^3.                  (3)

It preserves the fine/continuous block structure. The coarse lattice
becomes 4Z-2, with its same two occupied levels, and the fine lattice
spacing becomes 4h. The coarse fiber-area Jacobian is 16, so

    M'_h=64h^2,    delta'_h=2h,
    delta'_h/M'_h=1/(32h) -> infinity.                 (4)

Thus even after a full inner/outer-ball block normalization, relative
mesh need not be small. Before F, the exact ratio is
(h/2)/(4h^2)=1/(8h).

## 3. Exact sampled masses

Multiply the ordinary fine H_1 mixed measure by h; this common
positive factor does not change normalized depth. At z=0, for
u=i/L, -L<=i<=L, the interval length is epsilon(1+i/L). Thus

    mu_h(z=0)=h sum_i epsilon(1+i/L)=epsilon(2+h).       (5)

At z=1 the only fine u-levels are -h,0,h. The endpoint levels contain
only vertices. At u=0 the actual interval is

    Q_1 intersect {u=0}=[0,2h] in the x coordinate.

Consequently

    mu_h(z=1)=h(2h)=2epsilon,
    mu_h(total)=epsilon(4+h).                           (6)

In particular the largest fine interval has normalized mass
2/(4+h), tending to one half. Its midpoint is

    y_h=(1,0,h) in S_h.                                 (7)

## 4. Exact maximum depth and a five-cap certificate

The barycentric coordinates of Q_0 are

    lambda_A=(1-u)/2,
    lambda_B=(1+u)/4-x/(2epsilon),
    lambda_C=(1+u)/4+x/(2epsilon).

The three closed caps lambda_i>=1/3 cover Q_0, because the three
coordinates sum to one. Their sampled masses are all EXACTLY

    b_0=epsilon(8/9+2h/3)<=epsilon.                     (8)

Indeed the A-cap contains the full intervals with u<=1/3. The endpoint
1/3 is on the grid because L is divisible by three. The sum of their
lengths, multiplied by h, is epsilon(8/9+2h/3). The B-cap has length
epsilon(u+1/3) for u>=-1/3 and zero otherwise; summing the same
arithmetic progression gives (8). Reflection in x gives the C-cap.
The inequality in (8) is exactly h<=1/6.

These are actual ambient caps isolating the z=0 component: replace
their defining margins by lambda_i-1/3-Tz with T=2/epsilon. This is
strictly negative on Q_1. It leaves every value on Q_0 unchanged.

For z=1 write t=x-u/h. The two cuts t>=h and t<=h cover Q_1.
On its only positive fine interval u=0, each captures length h;
the boundary vertex points contribute zero H_1. Thus each cap has
sampled mass epsilon. To isolate this component, use the ambient
closed halfspaces with margins

    t-h-A(1-z),        h-t-A(1-z),
    A=2/h+2.

Both margins are strictly negative on Q_0 and retain the desired
cuts at z=1. Therefore FIVE actual closed ambient caps cover S_h,
each of sampled mass at most epsilon. They include all zero-length
boundary fibers in their coverage, even though those fibers add no
mass. It follows that every mixed point has normalized depth at most
epsilon/mu_h(total).

Conversely, every closed halfspace containing y_h restricts to its
own interval [0,2h] in at least a half-interval of length h. If its
continuous x-normal is zero, that entire interval is contained in
the cap. Thus every containing cap has sampled mass at least h^2.
Together with (6), this proves

    max_(y in S_h) depth_(mu_h)(y)
          =depth_(mu_h)(y_h)=1/(4+h).                    (9)

For comparison, the corresponding coarse mixed-area law has exact
maximal depth 2/9: its two equal-area triangle fibers are exposed in
the coarse base, so ordinary triangle centroid lower bounds and six
isolating barycentric caps give equality. Thus

    max fine depth ->1/4,      max coarse depth=2/9.

The original n=2,d=1 OC target is 1/8. Formula (9) is strictly above
it for this entire sequence.

## 5. A fixed cap already has nonvanishing normalized discrepancy

Take the fixed ambient halfspace H={x+2(z-1)>=0}. It excludes Q_0.
At z=1 it is the cut x>=0. The fine interval [0,2h] is entirely
included, so its normalized fine mass is 2/(4+h), tending to 1/2.
In Q_1 the negative cap isolates the vertex (-h,-1). Its two edge
intercept ratios are 1/2 and 1/(1+2h). Therefore

    coarse normalized mass of H
       =(1+4h)/[4(1+2h)] ->1/4.                         (10)

The fine/coarse normalized halfspace discrepancy does not tend to
zero, even though their TOTAL sampled and coarse masses have ratio
1+h/4 tending to one. The issue is directional sampling, not merely
an inaccurate total-mass approximation.

## 6. Further global block normalization cannot remove this scale gap

Suppose a convex body K satisfies B_2^3 subset K subset 6B_2^3, and
an affine map with linear part U sends K to a body containing B_2^3
and contained in R B_2^3, with fixed R. Widths give

    ||U||<=R,       sigma_min(U)>=1/6.                  (11)

The first uses the inner ball of K, the second its outer ball and
the inner ball of the image. Translations do not enter these bounds.
Thus no such further round normalization has an unbounded linear
condition number.

If the map preserves the original two-base/one-continuous block,
write its linear part as

    U=( B   0 )
      ( c'  d ),       B invertible, d!=0.

The fine base generator h e_u becomes h B e_u, and the coarse fiber
plane, generated by the fine and continuous directions, has area
Jacobian |B e_u||d|. Consequently its fine covering radius/coarse
mass ratio is multiplied EXACTLY by 1/|d|. Bounds (11) give
1/6<=|d|<=R. The divergent ratio in (4) therefore remains divergent
under every such uniformly round block normalization. This allows
rotation or shear of the two-dimensional base and arbitrary
base-to-continuous shear; it does not mix the continuous coordinate
into the base lattice.

In particular a common rescaling of the fine coordinate cancels out
of the ratio. Expanding only x enough to repair the ratio would make
the entire body unbounded or force loss of the fixed inball.

## 7. Component block normalization exposes a non-dense fine lattice

The two coarse bases are separate dependence components. Consider
their determinant-1/M_h block normalizations. For Q_0 one may use

    U=u,       X=x/(4epsilon).

Its residual triangle has area 1/2 and fixed shape, while its fine
mesh is h->0. For Q_1 use instead

    U=u/(2h),       X=(x-u/h)/(2h).                     (12)

This is block-preserving, has determinant 1/(4h^2)=1/M_h, and sends
Q_1 to conv{(-1/2,0),(1/2,0),(0,1)}, again of area 1/2. But its
fine mesh is EXACTLY 1/2, with covering radius 1/4.

This failure is independent of the choice of block normalizer. Any
map (u,x)->(a u,b u+d x), followed by translation, sends Q_1's fine
projection to an interval of length 2|a|h. If the transformed
triangle contains a fixed radius-rho ball, this width is at least
2rho. Hence its transformed lattice spacing |a|h is at least rho;
its covering radius is at least rho/2. No block normalization making
this component uniformly round can make its fine lattice dense.

Thus the example also identifies the genuine remaining case in a
componentwise mesh criterion: one positive coarse-mass component
has a transformed fine lattice of fixed mesh. A theorem ASSUMING
vanishing transformed meshes remains consistent with this example;
automatic satisfaction of that assumption would be false.

All rational areas, sampled sums, five-cap budgets, and fixed-cap
fractions are checked in `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_fine_mesh_coarse_mass_crossed_triangles.py`.
